metadata.description: Epoch-1 deploy receipt (R8A2): the schema-versioned record written in the user VibeVM state home after an applied deploy target — identity, provider, digests, scope, every owned resource with its post-apply digest, evidence, reversibility, prior-state handle, timestamps and final status (campaigns/packages-2026-09 architecture §7.2's exact list). `undeploy` removes only receipt-owned state. The receipt NEVER carries secrets: no prompts, no responses, no credential-bearing members exist on this shape. Generated Rust is the runtime receipt type.
Record schema epoch; 1 in epoch 1. The behaviour cell refuses every other value, so a newer receipt fails loudly instead of parsing into a wrong meaning.
The project (and optional package) identity the deployment belongs to.
The profile name that selected the target — backend-id grammar `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}`; validated by the behaviour cell.
The deploy target id — backend-id grammar; validated by the behaviour cell.
The generation of this target the receipt finalises; the prior generation lives in the intent journal.
The digest of the deployed artifact — exactly 64 lowercase hex, no `sha256:` prefix (one digest spelling across the three R8A2 records); validated by the behaviour cell.
The exact mechanism provider identity that applied the deployment.
The digest of the desired config the deployment reconciled to — exactly 64 lowercase hex; validated by the behaviour cell.
The destination scope — explicit, never inferred: privilege and blast radius read from here.
Every path/resource this deployment owns and its post-apply digest — the exact set `undeploy` may remove. An empty list is an explicit statement (a deployment owning no files), never an omission.
Whether the provider could undo this deployment. An installer that cannot roll back says so before apply; a receipt never implies a transaction its provider cannot provide.
When apply ran.
The final status. `applied` is mid-flight (written before independent verify); every terminal status finalises the receipt.
The provider evidence summary; non-blank and control-free; validated by the behaviour cell. Typed evidence kinds are the mechanism atom's to define — this member carries the summary a reader prints.
The handle under which the prior state survives for rollback; absent when there was none or the deployment is irreversible. Non-blank; validated by the behaviour cell.

When the receipt was finalised. The behaviour cell pins the matrix: present exactly for the terminal statuses (`verified`, `failed`, `rolled-back`) and absent for `applied`, because receipt finalisation is last.

A record's timestamp — a JTD `timestamp`, i.e. RFC 3339 on the wire, bound to `chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>` in code (the same binding the shared `timestamp` fragment and `hello`'s `world_sunset` carry). Spelled `"type": "timestamp"` and not `"type": "string"` because a bare string would give a date a SECOND legal spelling in the system, and one thing is written one way. Local to this schema: the record family is its only consumer, and a strict (`foreign_parsers = "none"`) schema must not pull a shared fragment the permissive formats also read.
The project/package identity a deployment belongs to — the half `undeploy` and reconciliation join receipts by.
The project identity; non-blank and control-free; validated by the behaviour cell.
The package identity when the deploy comes from one package rather than the host project; non-blank; validated by the behaviour cell.

The exact provider behind the deploy mechanism: the group-qualified key plus the version and content hash that make the identity reproducible. The same shape `artifact_record`'s producer carries — one provider-identity spelling across the R8A2 records.
The provider key in the ExtensionKey spelling `group/name#id`. Exactly one `/` before exactly one `#`, every component non-blank; validated by the behaviour cell.
The provider's own version string; non-blank. Deliberately not parsed here — the provider registry owns its grammar.
The provider's content hash in the one identity spelling `sha256:` + 64 lowercase hex — the same form every lockfile row carries; validated by the behaviour cell.
The four explicit destination scopes. `user` covers agent homes and `~/.vibe/bin`; `remote` a server; `system` an OS-level mutation behind a future privileged broker; `workspace` the project tree.
One resource this deployment owns after apply, at its post-apply digest.
The resource identity — an owned path or a named resource; non-blank and control-free; validated by the behaviour cell.
The digest observed after apply — exactly 64 lowercase hex; validated by the behaviour cell. `undeploy` refuses to erase a path whose digest moved away from this value.

The minimal closed final-status set §7.2 needs: `applied` (apply done, verify pending — receipt not finalised), `verified` (independent verify passed), `failed` (apply or verify refused; a multi-target saga records already-applied reversible targets as `rolled-back`), `rolled-back` (an inverse deployment returned the destination to its prior state).
